MULTI-SECTION EXPORT COMPLETE 2026-08-24. render-markdown.ts#buildRenderMarkdown now emits the full cv-document.ts scheme: `# Name`, the master's own contact line(s), `## Section`, `### Title — Org (Period)`, `- bullet`. Contact detail (email/phone/links) is extracted from the master markdown between the H1 and the first `## ` and re-emitted joined with ` | `, the same separator cv-document.ts splits on, which is what makes the confirmClaim re-render idempotent. Job titles are derived in code by fact-provenance.ts#parseEntryHeading (title, org, and period fall to null together whenever the heading does not clearly split as `Role — Company`) and carried on FactContext / cv_fact.title / FactSnapshot. Entry grouping key is now the (title, org, period) TRIPLE. Both writers verified end to end: extracted PDF text layer and DOCX word/document.xml both contain the contact parts and the titles, and both sha256s are stable across repeated renders.
No retry path after an export failure at approve: the application sits `approved` with `stateError` and cannot be re-approved (the state guard rejects non-in_review). Phase 5 candidate.
Bullet identity is text-string equality only — TailoredBullet has no stable id, so two overreach bullets with identical text in one render are indistinguishable to confirmClaim and the approval gate.

LinkedIn Description granularity FIXED 2026-08-24: linkedin.importer.ts#splitDescription emits one markdown list item per claim (author's own bullets/newlines win; otherwise a deterministic sentence split that skips decimals, initials, and abbreviations), so a role no longer extracts as one paragraph-sized fact. Known under-split: a sentence ending in a URL path segment ("Visit https://a.b/c. Then...") stays as one claim, because the final token reads as a single-letter initial. Under-splitting keeps a whole claim intact, so it is the safe direction; revisit only if it shows up in real exports.

SCHEMA GAP RESOLVED 2026-08-24. ExtractedFact/ContextualFact/FactSnapshot/cv_fact now carry {section, title, org, period}. Mapping is by normalised text (the same normalisation hashFactContent uses): exact match first, then containment either way with a 12-char floor so a short token like "Py" cannot match an arbitrary line. Where several matching blocks DISAGREE on a field it is nulled per-field, so a bullet duplicated under two employers still keeps its shared section. Unmapped facts are logged at warn with counts and truncated text, never thrown — a heading-less CV is a valid input. Derived context is deliberately OUTSIDE contentHash (pinned by tests in fact-identity.spec.ts and fact-provenance.spec.ts): re-titling a job heading must not orphan every fact under it.

Facts extracted before 2026-08-24 have cv_fact.title NULL (AddFactTitle1756700000000 deliberately does not backfill — a guessed job title is fabrication). They render title-less as `### — Org (Period)` until the master CV is next saved and re-extracted. Not a defect; noted so a title-less entry on an old application is not mistaken for a derivation bug.

Phase 4 export renders one 'Tailored Highlights' section: SUPERSEDED. Exports are now real multi-section CVs with per-entry title/org/period. What is still missing structurally is anything the fact graph does not carry at all — e.g. a location line per entry, or ordering entries by date rather than by first appearance in the bullet array.

pdf-parse's bundled pdf.js throws inside Jest's node environment for ANY PDF (verified with a bare jest config, no ts-jest or Nest involved). Production is unaffected. cv-pdf.service.spec.ts shells out to a child node process to assert extracted text — anyone calling pdf-parse live under Jest will hit this.

pdfkit's built-in Helvetica is WinAnsi-only: CJK, emoji, and Arabic silently corrupt in PDF output. CvPdfService now RAISES on unencodable characters, naming them and pointing at DOCX (which renders them correctly). Real Unicode font support is deferred — needs an embedded TTF, a licence decision, and a Docker image change.

pdfkit hashes info.CreationDate into the PDF /ID trailer, so an unpinned CreationDate makes the sha256 wall-clock dependent. It is pinned to new Date(0) because spec §6.3 reuses that sha256 for artifact idempotency.

LinkedIn Positions.csv Description routinely contains newlines inside quoted fields. Reading the CSV line-at-a-time shredded such a row into a phantom extra position (`### Role — <prose fragment>`) — a job the candidate never held, invented by the parser. parseCsv now splits records via splitCsvRecords (quote-aware); never reintroduce a body.split(/\r?\n/) there.

cv_fact.section/title/org/period are DERIVED IN CODE from the markdown headings (src/master/fact-provenance.ts), never asked of the extraction model, and never part of contentHash. Do not add them to fact-extractor.service.ts OUTPUT_SCHEMA or SYSTEM_PROMPT: a model naming the employer or date range fabricates on the fields an employer judges a CV by (spec 6). Null means "could not be confidently mapped" and must render as nothing downstream — never fall back to a nearby heading.

A tailored entry with NEITHER title, org, nor period still emits a bare `### —` heading. This is load-bearing, not cosmetic: cv-document.ts attaches a bullet to the most recently opened entry, so an unattributed group written with no heading of its own after `### Senior Developer — Acme (2019-2024)` is read as more of Acme's work — a real employer and role stamped onto a bullet the fact graph never connected to it. Caught by a test in render-markdown.spec.ts; never 'simplify' the bare heading away. Both writers suppress it (they emit a heading only when a title or org is present), so it never reaches the PDF/DOCX page.

buildRenderMarkdown ordering is deterministic BY CONTRACT: sections, entries, and bullets are all ordered by first appearance in the bullets array, with the 'Additional Highlights' catch-all forced last; the facts array is a lookup only, so its order cannot influence the bytes. Spec §6.3 reuses the artifact sha256 for idempotency, so a Map/object iteration whose order could vary would defeat pdfkit's pinned CreationDate just as thoroughly as a wall-clock timestamp. Pinned by tests in render-markdown.spec.ts.

buildRenderMarkdown's contact block is re-extracted from its OWN prior output on the confirmClaim path, so the emitted form must be the canonical one: parts trimmed, whitespace-collapsed, and joined with ` | ` on a single line between the H1 and the first `## `. Any other join (a different separator, one part per line, a trailing space) makes pass 2 differ from pass 1 and silently changes the artifact sha256 spec §6.3 depends on. Pinned by a three-pass test in render-markdown.spec.ts.

A derived job title is user-authored text written into a `### ` heading, so render-markdown.ts#normalizeHeadingField collapses its whitespace and rewrites any em dash to a hyphen before emitting. An em dash inside a title would make cv-document.ts re-parse `### Lead — Deputy — Acme (2019)` as an ambiguous heading and silently relabel the employer; a newline would break the one-heading-per-line parse. Neutralised rather than dropped — losing a real title is a silent loss, mangling the employer is a fabrication.

Entry grouping is keyed on the (title, org, period) TRIPLE, not (org, period). A promotion inside one company over the same period is two real CV entries; keying without the title merged them and discarded one job title. Nulls are values in that key, not wildcards: a title-less bullet never joins a titled entry at the same employer.
